title: Faulty Keyboard
statement: You type the characters of `s` one after another on a broken keyboard, starting from an empty screen. Every letter other than `'i'` is added to the end of the text as usual, but pressing `'i'` adds nothing and instead flips the whole text currently on the screen end to end. Return the text shown once all of `s` has been typed.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The direct simulation reverses the whole screen at every `'i'`, which costs O(n) each time and O(n²) overall. Reversing is not really needed: we can just remember **which way** the text currently faces. While it faces normally, a new letter goes on the right end; while it is flipped, a letter typed at the screen's end lands on the left end of the unflipped text. A double-ended buffer (two arrays, `front` grown leftwards and `back` grown rightwards) supports both in O(1).

## Approach

1. Keep `front` (letters added on the left, stored in push order), `back` (letters added on the right) and a `flipped` flag.
2. For each character `ch`: an `'i'` toggles `flipped`.
3. Any other letter goes to `front` when `flipped` is true, otherwise to `back`.
4. The unflipped text is `front` reversed followed by `back`.
5. If the screen is flipped at the end, reverse that text once, then join it.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "string"`. `s`, `t`, `r` go to `back`: `back = [s, t, r]`. The `'i'` sets `flipped = true`. Then `n` and `g` go to `front`: `front = [n, g]`. The unflipped text is `[g, n] + [s, t, r]` = `"gnstr"`; the screen is flipped, so reverse it to get `"rtsng"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character is handled once, plus one final reverse.
- Space: O(n) for the two buffers.

## Pitfalls

- An `'i'` is never written to the screen; it only flips the text.
- An even number of `'i'`s in a row cancel out, so the final orientation matters, not the count.
- When flipped, a typed letter belongs on the **left** of the stored text, not the right.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `front` | letters added to the left end, in the order they were typed |
| `back` | letters added to the right end |
| `flipped` | whether the screen currently shows the stored text reversed |
| `ch` | the character being typed |
| `text` | the stored text rebuilt from both buffers |

narration.2: front collects letters that belong on the left end of the stored text.
narration.3: back collects letters that belong on the right end.
narration.4: flipped records whether the screen shows the stored text reversed.
narration.6: Type the characters one by one.
narration.8: ...it only flips the orientation of the screen.
narration.9: While flipped, the screen's end is the left end of the stored text.
narration.10: So the letter is added on the left.
narration.12: Otherwise the letter simply goes on the right end.
narration.16: Rebuild the stored text: left additions in reverse order, then right additions.
narration.17: If the screen ends up flipped, the visible text is the reverse.
narration.20: Join the characters into the final screen text.
